about.title: About Me
about.subtitle: My journey, philosophy, and what drives me

whoIAm.title: Who I Am
whoIAm.p1: In mid-2025 I found myself missing a few things: a psychologist, order in my daily life, and a partner for the startup I was building at the time. I'm an empath: greedy for meaning and bad at holding on to specifics — I needed a system to remember for me. That's how Imperia OS was born — I now live and work inside it every day.
whoIAm.p2: I don't play roles and I don't hide behind jargon. What matters most to me in an agent system is being able to say why it did what it did — so I build the flow out of steps that can be named, not out of a model's improvisation. My strength lies in
whoIAm.p2Emphasis: transparency and the ability to face hard truths
whoIAm.p2End: , both in code and in collaboration.
whoIAm.quote: Mind brings clarity. Heart brings depth. Presence is my gift.

journey.title: The Journey
journey.p1: I graduated from LNMO (Laboratory of Continuous Mathematical Education) in St. Petersburg, where I explored over a dozen programming languages, from Pascal to OCaml, C, Haskell, and even Brainfuck. From my school years, I was involved in scientific research and presented at academic conferences. I placed 3rd in Mathematics at ICYS-2012 in the Netherlands, 1st at the St. Petersburg State Competition, and 3rd at the Baltic Science and Engineering Competition. In 2015-2016, I served on the youth jury for the Baltic competition. During this time, I worked on information decomposition algorithms, neural networks, and data analysis.
journey.p2: My path in development has been shaped by a principle:
journey.p2Emphasis: life is a continuous stream of experience that makes you stronger and wiser
journey.p2End: . Each project is an opportunity to learn, not just about technology, but about how systems serve people.
journey.p3: I used to approach problems from my head, chasing control and perfect solutions. Over time, I learned that true engineering happens when you stay present with the problem, listen deeply, and act from understanding rather than avoidance. The best architectures emerge when you respect both technical constraints and human needs.
journey.p4: From dynamic EAV systems a decade ago to Hyperledger Fabric at Sber and IBM, to serverless Go on AWS, to the agent platform I build today, I've learned that sustainable solutions come from discipline, patience, and a willingness to stay with complexity until clarity emerges.

approach.title: My Approach
approach.p1End: . There are no shortcuts to quality. That holds for agents more than for anything else I've built: a stateful agent here is a state machine — the algorithm controls the flow, and each step is atomic, one LLM call or one deterministic operation. The algorithm doesn't hallucinate; only the bounded steps inside it can. Stateless agents are the rest: one call, no machine.
approach.p2End: . Control is an illusion; you can't predict every edge case or prevent every bug. But you can take full ownership of your decisions, your code quality, and the trust you build with your team — and you can leave behind a system that records what it did, so the next person doesn't have to take your word for it.
approach.p3End: . A knowledge graph follows the development flow — business use cases first, tests written from them, code implementing them, all three indexed and embedded automatically — so whatever already exists is visible before anything new gets written, and Clean Architecture keeps every module portable enough to use anywhere. That isn't a formality; it is care for future maintainers, including yourself six months from now when you've forgotten why you made that choice.
approach.p4End: to my work. Not just technical attention, but genuine engagement with the problem at hand. Great engineering happens when you stop avoiding complexity and start listening to what the system is telling you.

currentFocus.title: Current Focus
currentFocus.p1: Imperia OS is where my attention goes. Two kinds of memory back the development, and both reach the agent the same two ways: pulled into its prompt automatically by embedding match, or fetched on demand through MCP tools. The first is the knowledge graph over use cases, tests and code. The second is a thought system — a hierarchy that composes itself, where every new thought is summarized into the layer above, recursively. The same module runs the business agents.
currentFocus.p2: Underneath, the system reduces to three abstractions. Agents are one. Blocks are the second — everything addressable shares one shape and one embedding. Protocols are the third — everything that crosses a boundary, payment included: paid access is a decorator over the protocol, and the same slot accepts signing, audit, or a blockchain commitment.

beyondCode.title: Beyond Code
beyondCode.p1: Outside of programming, I'm interested in mindfulness practices, physical training, and the philosophy of continuous improvement. I believe that maintaining balance between focus and rest, intensity and ease, makes me a better engineer.
beyondCode.p2: These interests aren't separate from my work; they inform how I approach problems. Attention, patience, and presence are as important in debugging a complex system as they are in any other practice.

continuousLearning.title: Continuous Learning:
continuousLearning.text: Every experience is an opportunity to grow. I treat each project as a chance to learn something new about systems, people, or myself.

curiosity.title: Curiosity:
curiosity.text: Asking "why" and "how" leads to better solutions. I dig deep into problems to understand root causes, not just symptoms.

progress.title: Progress Over Perfection:
progress.text: Step by step, without rushing. Sustainable progress beats flashy shortcuts every time.

trust.title: Trust and Care:
trust.text: Building trust through reliability, clear communication, and genuine care for the people I work with and the systems we maintain together.

balance.title: Balance:
balance.text: Technical excellence matters, but so does pragmatism. Innovation is important, but so is stability. Finding harmony between competing needs is where real engineering happens.

imperiaOs.title: Imperia OS
imperiaOs.subtitle: An AI assistant to do everything its user wants — and the platform that goal requires.

problem.title: The Problem
problem.text: Most AI integrations give a model a prompt and hope for the best. No workflow discipline, no memory that survives the call, no audit trail — no way to know why the agent did what it did.

solution.title: The Approach
solution.text: The algorithm controls the flow, not the LLM. A stateful agent is a state machine: each step is atomic — one LLM call or one deterministic operation — so the algorithm doesn't hallucinate; only the bounded steps inside it can. Stateless agents are the rest: one call, no machine. Every step is recorded — what was observed, what was missing, why this way.

steps: Business use cases come first — the spec tree is runtime configuration
Tests are written from the use cases — verify before implementation
Code implements them, and all three layers are indexed into the knowledge graph and embedded automatically
Memory reaches the agent two ways — pulled into its prompt by embedding match, or fetched on demand through MCP tools

imperia-os.title: Imperia OS — An AI Assistant and the Platform It Requires
imperia-os.description: Agent platform with a state-machine runtime, a knowledge graph over the development flow, and two kinds of memory reaching the agent through MCP.
imperia-os.problem: Giving an LLM full control doesn't scale. It decides what to do, which tools to call, when to stop — and it keeps nothing between calls. No memory, no business context, no traceability, no way to prevent the agent from editing code before it understands the problem.
imperia-os.solution: The algorithm controls the flow. A stateful agent is a state machine: each step is atomic — one LLM call or one deterministic operation. Memory reaches the agent two ways: pulled into its prompt automatically by embedding match, or fetched on demand through MCP tools. Everything the system does reduces to three abstractions — agents, blocks and protocols.
technicalDetails: State-machine runtime — the algorithm sequences the steps; an LLM call is one bounded step among deterministic ones
Knowledge graph over the development flow — business use cases, the tests written from them, and the code implementing them, all indexed and embedded
Thought system — a self-composing hierarchy where every new thought is summarized into the layer above; the same module runs the business agents
MCP tools — typed, on-demand access to the same memory the prompt receives automatically
Three abstractions — agents; blocks, where everything addressable shares one shape and one embedding; protocols, for everything that crosses a boundary
Paid access as a decorator over the protocol — the same slot accepts signing, audit, or a blockchain commitment
results: The same infrastructure builds the platform and delivers it to its users
Re-use is the default — the knowledge map shows what already exists before anything new is written, and Clean Architecture keeps every module portable
Every agent decision is traceable — the record holds what was observed, what was missing, and why the agent chose its approach
lessonsLearned: LLMs become reliable when an algorithm controls the flow — the algorithm doesn't hallucinate, only the bounded steps inside it can
Separate stores beat one merged store — code structure, agent memory and user data need different schemas and query patterns
Payment belongs in a decorator over the protocol, not inside the agent — the same slot then takes signing, audit or a blockchain commitment

mobile-platform.title: Cross-Platform Mobile Platform
mobile-platform.description: Scalable mobile platform on Flutter and AWS with clean architecture and automated infrastructure.
mobile-platform.problem: Needed a foundation for a cross-platform product with reliable backend and automated deployment. Typical approaches led to fragmented architecture.
mobile-platform.solution: Implemented Clean Architecture with Feature-based structure in Flutter. Backend - serverless on AWS (Lambda in Golang). Infrastructure defined in CDK and deploys automatically.
technicalDetails: Clean Architecture + feature-based modules, event-driven reactive layout, Riverpod for state
Serverless backend on AWS — Lambda in Go, DynamoDB with composite keys, S3 for media, Amplify and Cognito for auth
lessonsLearned: Clean Architecture pays off on large projects
Infrastructure as Code is critical for reproducibility

website-builder.title: Dynamic Website Builder Platform
website-builder.description: Flexible website builder system with dynamic data schema and multi-tenancy support.
website-builder.problem: Needed a builder where users can create arbitrary entity types and fields without DB migrations. Plus data isolation between clients.
website-builder.solution: Implemented EAV (Entity-Attribute-Value) pattern with multi-tenancy at the database level. Users create their entities and fields through the interface, data is stored in a universal and extensible structure.
technicalDetails: EAV pattern for dynamic schema without migrations
Multi-tenancy with isolated databases per client
Type-safe storage of different data types
results: Users create entities without developer involvement
System adapts to different business domains
lessonsLearned: EAV provides maximum flexibility but requires query optimization
Multi-tenancy at DB level is the most reliable isolation
